title: The Valencia Cabaret and Leon Rappolo sitting in
summary: Hug played little groups at the Valencia Cabaret on Bourbon Street, with Eddie Miller, and Rappolo once sat in.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: And then you went and played in the French Quarter for a while, I guess.

I went to work at a cabaret. It was called the Cabarets in those days. It was called the Valencia Cabaret. It was where the Royal Sinesta Hotel is today, on Bourbon Street. And I worked with various little groups, three-piece groups there, from time to time. Some of the musicians I played with there was Chink Morton's son, Chink Morton Jr. Eddie Miller played there with me for a while. Who's now playing with Pete Fountain. Yes. And Eddie played alto sax in those days. He wasn't playing tenor. And Al Hesman, banjo player. I'll never forget the night that Leonor Pola, a famous Rhythm Kings clarinet player, came in town. He was hospitalized, you know, for many years.

And he was out on pass or something. And he stopped in. And I have just a very, very faint recollection of him sitting in with me, you know, and playing. But, of course, this was a very great thrill for me to know just the fact. I remember that I know he sat in. And I couldn't tell you too much about his playing because, as I say, it was a long time ago, you know. But I do know that he came in there and sat down with us and played a couple of sets, you know.
